- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) and model forecasts are flat or rising slowly, adjust upward by 2–5% to account for sentiment-driven momentum.  
- After a sharp spike in price (e.g., >10% from prior period), model tends to overcorrect; reduce forecast slope by 10–20% for next 3–5 periods to avoid overshoot.  
- If official supply net is negative and bearish sentiment dominates (≥0.67), model often underestimates downside risk; add 3–8% downward bias to forecast mean.  
- When event count is high and supply net is negative, model tends to overestimate bullishness; apply downward correction proportional to bearish sentiment weight (e.g., 1.5x bearish sentiment → 1.5x downward adjustment).  
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model often fails to mean-revert; apply a 1–3% smoothing filter toward historical mean over 10–15 periods.  
- For 30-day forecasts with high event density, reduce forecast volatility by 20–30% to reflect reduced predictability from exogenous shocks.
